title: Largest Swing of Any Slice Sum
statement:
You get an integer array nums that may contain negative numbers. For any contiguous slice, take the absolute value of its sum.

Return the largest such absolute value. The empty slice is allowed and has sum 0, so the answer is never negative.

examples.why: The slice [-5, 1, -4] sums to -8, and |-8| = 8. The best positive slice only reaches 3, and the whole array sums to -6.
The whole array sums to 6; dropping the -1 is not allowed because the slice must be contiguous.
All negative: the most negative slice is the whole array, -5.

hints: The absolute value of a sum is large when the sum is very positive or very negative. Can you find both separately?
The largest slice sum is the classic running-best (Kadane) scan. Run a mirrored version for the smallest slice sum.
Even simpler: a slice sum is prefix[j] − prefix[i]. The largest absolute difference between any two prefix sums is max(prefix) − min(prefix), with prefix 0 included.

explain.intuition:
|sum| is big either because the sum is very large or very small. So the answer is the larger of the best maximum slice sum and the negated best minimum slice sum. Both come from one Kadane-style pass: keep the best sum of a slice ending at the current index, and either extend it or start fresh.

The prefix-sum view is even shorter. Every slice sum is a difference P[j] − P[i] of two prefix sums. Its absolute value does not care which comes first, so the best is simply the gap between the largest and the smallest prefix sum, counting the empty prefix 0. Think of a stock chart: the biggest move in either direction is from its lowest point to its highest, whichever happened first.
steps: Keep a running prefix sum p, starting at 0, and its maximum hi and minimum lo, both starting at 0.
For each number, add it to p and update hi and lo.
pitfalls: Running only the maximum-sum Kadane. A big negative slice like in the first example is missed.
Taking |total sum| or the sum of absolute values. The slice must be contiguous and signs do not flip.
Starting hi and lo at prefix[1] instead of 0, which drops slices that start at index 0.

solutions.title: Every slice
solutions.idea: Extend each start one element at a time and track the largest absolute sum.

solutions.title: Kadane for the max and the min
solutions.idea: Track the best sum ending here in both directions; the answer is the larger magnitude.

solutions.title: Highest minus lowest prefix sum
solutions.idea: Any slice sum is a difference of two prefix sums, so the largest absolute one is max prefix − min prefix.

followups: Return the slice's start and end too.
The array is circular, so a slice may wrap from the end to the start. What changes?
